full_judgment: 9. The main object of the State Acquisition Act 1950 was to eliminate all kinds of rent-receiving interests and make the Government the sole landlord and create only one class of tenants, who would be styled as "maliks", Section 75A of the Act, which was enacted in 1954, purported to prevent, after some steps had been taken for the purpose of the preparation of the compensation assessment roll, the creation of any rent receiving interest other than those which were already existing. All rent receiving interests as well as all non-retainable lands of the rent receivers were acquired under a notification under section 3 of the Act with effect from 14-4-56 and thereafter the excess khas lands as well as the non-retainable khas land of non-rent receivers were acquired on the publication of the compensation assessment roll made under Chapter V of Part IV of the Act. Part V of the Act, which contains provisions relating to the rights and liabilities of the tenants under the Government after the elimination of all kinds of rent-receivers, came into force in different areas on different dates.
